milestones.title: M1 — Megabonk on Apple Silicon without Rosetta
milestones.description: Qualify a coherent, source-buildable Pear runtime on a declared Apple Silicon/macOS configuration. Required evidence: normal macOS execution permissions; complete required process/module path without Rosetta; Steam, input, audio and save/relaunch behavior; at least 20 minutes of active gameplay; reproducible build/setup and known limitations. This is not a general end-user release or a claim of performance superiority. Architecture: docs/architecture.md. No due date is assumed.

milestones.title: R1 — Evaluate an independent Pear CPU translator
milestones.description: Optional research alongside M1. Explain a concrete reason to change the CPU backend, compare a declared semantic subset using Cranelift and an appropriate reference, then decide whether further runtime/Wine integration is justified. Research may conclude with a documented decision to retain FEX; later conditional experiments may be closed as not planned. R1 does not block M1 and does not commit Pear to a Rust rewrite.

issues.title: Qualify source availability and pin the runtime toolchain
issues.purpose: A commercial demonstration and public source snapshots do not yet establish a reproducible Pear runtime.
scope: Inventory Wine, FEX, DXMT, dependencies, exact public revisions, required downstream patches and build tools.
Audit the chosen source archives/trees and relevant public changes, including CrossOver source availability where relevant; identify missing macOS behavior.
Record per-component license/notice requirements and contribution policies before copying or distributing code.
acceptance: A source manifest identifies immutable revisions, archive/patch hashes and build-tool versions, with evidence for every required component.
A gap table separates reusable code, patches to implement, unavailable inputs and external prerequisites.
No opaque preview binary or placeholder hash is classified as a reproducible input; a no-go finding is explicit and downstream work remains blocked.

issues.title: Probe macOS ABI, memory, JIT and signing capabilities
issues.purpose: The Darwin host contract is a fundamental engineering gate that Rust or a different code generator cannot remove.
scope: Build a small ARM64 probe for x18 mode transitions, page size and protection, low address mapping, thread memory-order mode, and JIT publication.
Test normal supported signing/provisioning with system protections enabled; distinguish API presence from successful operation.
Document developer execution and general user distribution separately, including account/profile prerequisites and unresolved restrictions.
acceptance: Versioned source, commands and redacted results report each capability as passed, failed or unavailable on the declared Mac/OS.
Nested callbacks, signals and failure exits preserve guest/host ABI state; 4 KiB semantics and per-thread policy are verified rather than assumed.
Every prerequisite for the declared M1 configuration passes through a normal signed path; any distribution limitation is explicit and cannot be described as a general release.

issues.title: Define runtime contracts and choose the manager language
issues.purpose: Pear needs stable ownership and component boundaries before selecting a launcher implementation language.
scope: Define versioned runtime-lock, game-profile, launch, failure and qualification-record schemas.
Compare Rust and Swift for the same small manifest/child-process/logging task; include packaging, FFI, dependencies and contributor cost.
Keep CPU, Wine and graphics code in their existing languages; specify prefix/cache/data ownership and bounded profile operations.
acceptance: Schemas and examples clearly distinguish proposed, built, tested and supported states without invented hashes or results.
An architecture decision records the manager language and evidence; Rust is not chosen merely for presumed game speed.
Unknown versions, incompatible component families, unsafe paths and invalid profile operations have defined rejection behavior.

issues.title: Bring up the ARM64 Wine host and macOS ABI boundary
issues.purpose: The current x64 Wine host cannot satisfy Rosetta independence, and ARM64 macOS support must be qualified from source.
scope: Build the selected Wine revision as an ARM64 macOS host with required PE architectures and matching tools.
Implement or integrate missing loader, address-layout, x18 transition, thread/signal and Mac-driver changes as attributable patches.
Exercise host/guest/native callback boundaries before attempting a complete game.
acceptance: A clean ARM64 host build and minimal PE/API fixtures run with documented normal permissions.
Patch rationale, sources and build commands are recorded; no Intel host loader is silently selected.
Thread entry, nested callbacks, error exits and exception-context capture have targeted regression evidence.

issues.title: Port FEX Wine host services to Darwin and integrate its CPU modules
issues.purpose: FEX has reusable Windows CPU modules, but its inspected Wine Unix library contains Linux-specific services and build assumptions.
scope: Port the required Source/Windows/UnixLib host services and build rules, including memory-order controls, using an explicit Darwin boundary.
Integrate ARM64EC and, where required, WoW64 emulator modules into the matching Wine build.
Preserve guest-state, exception, suspend, guard-page and code-invalidation semantics; avoid a wholesale Linux-userspace port.
acceptance: Small x64 PE programs execute through the recorded FEX module in the ARM64 Wine host with no Rosetta fallback.
Required host services have regression tests and documented thread/JIT/exception ownership.
The patch series builds from the P01 lock, and upstream contribution policy is respected independently of downstream reuse rights.

issues.title: Qualify CPU semantics and the Wine translation boundary
issues.purpose: A menu or arithmetic demo cannot expose subtle CPU, threading, ABI and exception errors.
scope: Adapt suitable redistributable CPU fixtures and compare defined register/flag/memory/fault outcomes with a native x86-64 or validated independent reference.
Cover partial registers, relevant SIMD/float operations, atomics, memory ordering, TLS, callbacks, faults/SEH, guard pages and changed executable code.
Test x86/WoW64 helpers or explicitly establish which parts remain unsupported; do not infer memory ordering from single-thread tests.
acceptance: The declared fixture suite passes or records explicit unsupported coverage; required-path failures are not waived.
Memory-ordering and multithread stress tests run with the actual per-thread policy; FEX tests that disable TSO are not used as proof of TSO correctness.
Failures reduce to reproducible fixtures with the Wine/FEX/host boundary identified.

issues.title: Reproduce the ARM64EC DXMT and ARM64 Metal bridge build
issues.purpose: Existing ARM64EC CI is a starting point, but Pear needs a coherent Wine/DXMT ABI and reproducible native dependencies.
scope: Pin DXMT, submodules, LLVM, llvm-mingw, Wine build interfaces and SDK settings using actual upstream CI/source.
Build the ARM64EC Windows DLLs and paired native winemetal/Metal/shader-conversion dependencies.
Inventory native slices, PE variants, DLL modes, driver exports, notices and output hashes.
acceptance: A clean build produces a complete versioned artifact set with architecture and dependency reports.
Wine driver exports and winemetal pairing are documented and verified against the chosen Wine port.
No claim of runtime compatibility is based solely on successful compilation or an upstream artifact.

issues.title: Qualify Direct3D 11 through the native Metal path
issues.purpose: Graphics correctness needs independent fixtures before debugging Unity or interpreting game frame rates.
scope: Run redistributable x64 D3D11 fixtures for device creation, buffers/textures, shaders/compute, depth/blend, readback, swapchain, resize and presentation.
Exercise native callbacks, lifetime synchronization and repeated device creation across Wine/FEX/DXMT.
Record actual DLL/backend selection and classify unsupported required features.
acceptance: Expected images/readback results and lifecycle behavior pass the published fixture suite.
The module inventory proves the intended DXMT/Metal path without silent renderer substitution.
Targeted validation logs are retained; correctness validation layers are excluded from later performance runs.

issues.title: Implement the native runtime supervisor and Megabonk profile
issues.purpose: The runtime must be launched predictably without inheriting the fixed paths and assumptions of the original experiment.
scope: Implement the chosen native manager/CLI, manifest verification, explicit launch arguments, scoped environment, prefix ownership and structured failures.
Define App ID 3405340 and the known executable in a versioned Megabonk profile; preserve game and user-data boundaries.
Use a fixture child to develop supervision before the full runtime is available; prepare isolated prefix/manual recovery instructions.
acceptance: Tests cover version/path rejection, child exit/crash, logging redaction and prefix isolation.
Runtime files remain immutable and unrelated Wine processes/prefixes are not terminated.
The profile records unknown or untested features accurately; a polished GUI and automatic save rollback are not prerequisites.

issues.title: Collect complete process and module evidence of Rosetta independence
issues.purpose: An ARM64 launcher or file header alone cannot establish that Steam and every required helper avoid Rosetta.
scope: Implement native collection of runtime identities, process lifetimes and required loaded host/guest modules.
Distinguish Mach-O running slices and translation state from guest PE x64/i386 execution through FEX.
Capture startup, detached/short-lived helpers where required, game play, exit and relaunch; report observation gaps.
acceptance: Positive and negative fixtures demonstrate that required Intel host execution is detected rather than silently ignored.
Per-process evidence is attributed correctly; sysctl.proc_translated from a parent shell is not used for children.
The redacted report contains no credentials or whole process environments and fails qualification when a required path is translated or unobserved.

issues.title: Validate Windows Steam and its helper architecture requirements
issues.purpose: Steam is part of the required runtime, and its installed package includes both x64 and i386 components.
scope: Validate official Steam login, startup/update and normal App 3405340 launch in the candidate runtime.
Observe required helpers and DLLs dynamically; provide required WoW64/x86 support or demonstrate its absence from the supported path.
Keep native macOS Steam bridging as a separately justified alternative; preserve the original Steam API and ownership behavior.
acceptance: Normal Steam launch initializes the game's Steam integration without substituting a success stub or shipping steam_appid.txt as the supported route.
Steam build, required child/module architectures and FEX mode are recorded with no required Rosetta process.
Optional overlay/cloud/achievement/Discord behavior is tested or explicitly marked untested; login state is never committed.

issues.title: Qualify Megabonk gameplay, input, audio and save/relaunch behavior
issues.purpose: The milestone requires real gameplay and persistence, not a menu screenshot.
scope: Run the declared game version on the source-built candidate with at least 20 minutes of active play and recorded escalating workload.
Test keyboard/mouse, menus, pause/resume, focus, audio, settings, local save, clean exit and reload using backed-up test data.
Test controllers and other optional integrations only when claimed by the supported profile; preserve explicit untested status otherwise.
acceptance: The documented run meets the active-play duration and records the actual scenes/workload, defects, resolution and settings.
Progress/settings survive normal exit and relaunch; three clean launch/exit cycles are recorded.
Required features pass; no game binary patch or uncontrolled fallback is used to hide a runtime failure.

issues.title: Assemble and reproduce the signed Pear runtime candidate
issues.purpose: A coherent, source-buildable engine must be reproducible without hidden commercial files or machine-specific state.
scope: Build the complete candidate from a clean environment using the runtime lock and ordered patch series.
Package matching CPU/API/graphics components, notices, source references and signing requirements as one immutable runtime artifact.
Repeat the build/setup and compare unsigned payloads or document nondeterministic inputs separately from signing.
acceptance: A second clean setup reproduces the declared configuration using documented source and prerequisites.
The architecture/signature/dependency inventory has no required Intel-only host component or undocumented copied binary.
Developer execution and wider distribution status are separately stated; end-user installer completion is not implied.

issues.title: Add regression CI and a maintained upstream patch workflow
issues.purpose: Pear needs a repeatable way to detect regressions and maintain ports after the first successful run.
scope: Run schema/build checks and redistributable fixtures in appropriate CI; distinguish portable tests from real macOS hardware qualification.
Document patch provenance, rebase rules, last passing versions and per-project contribution restrictions.
Keep proprietary games and authenticated Steam environments in opt-in local qualification rather than public CI inputs.
acceptance: A deliberately failing fixture is detected and an incompatible runtime/profile cannot be promoted.
The candidate build/qualification report links test and source revisions with known coverage gaps.
No secret, proprietary game, credentialed prefix or generated upstream submission is introduced by the workflow.

issues.title: Characterize frame times, stability and power under controlled conditions
issues.purpose: The first supported configuration needs observable quality and limitations; no performance advantage is presumed.
scope: Record actual resolution, graphics/FPS/VSync settings, scene, cache state, power source, Game Mode, Low Power Mode and thermal conditions.
Collect frame-time distribution/stalls, startup, memory and available power/thermal measurements with repeated runs where practical.
Keep paused/menu, early and later gameplay distinct; compare the old Rosetta baseline only when the conditions can actually be matched.
acceptance: A reproducible protocol and non-sensitive raw/summary results identify workload differences and measurement limits.
HUD snapshots are not reported as frame-time distributions and system power is not labeled game-only power.
No fixed superiority target or comparative claim is needed to close the issue; serious playability defects feed back to the runtime/game issues.

issues.title: Publish the first Rosetta-free Megabonk qualification record
issues.purpose: Close the product milestone only when its complete evidence and reproducibility requirements are met.
scope: Consolidate source/build, signing, process/module, graphics, Steam, gameplay, persistence and quality evidence.
Reproduce the supported setup independently or in a second documented clean environment and record remaining distribution limitations.
Update README and the game profile to the exact tested scope and link all prerequisite issues.
acceptance: All required M1 gates pass, including at least 20 minutes of active gameplay and no required Rosetta process.
P10, P12 and P15 execution evidence identifies the same final runtime-lock/artifact, profile, game and Steam versions as P13; any relevant change requires requalification.
Any observation gap or required-feature failure keeps the issue and milestone open.
The support claim names tested versions/hardware and limitations; it does not generalize one configuration to all Macs or imply an end-user release.

issues.title: Define the CPU-engine hypothesis and differential semantics corpus
issues.purpose: An independent translator needs a specific reason to exist and an oracle for guest behavior before backend experiments are meaningful.
scope: Choose a falsifiable platform/interface/correctness/performance hypothesis and separate CPU translation from graphics/API/game bottlenecks.
Declare an initial x64 subset, guest-state contract and fault/undefined-output policy.
Build redistributable reference fixtures using native x86-64 and/or independently validated implementations; audit reuse of FEX tests.
acceptance: The hypothesis, reference results, declared subset and unsupported cases are reviewable.
Defined registers/flags/memory/faults are compared and discrepancies minimized; finite tests are not presented as global equivalence.
If no defensible hypothesis remains, document retaining FEX and stop dependent research rather than inventing a speed claim.

issues.title: Compare Cranelift with a reference CPU-code backend
issues.purpose: Cranelift should be evaluated as a code-generation component, not assumed to be a complete x64 emulator.
scope: Implement a bounded semantic frontend and feed equivalent behavior to Cranelift and a justified reference backend.
Measure translation latency, generated size, dispatch cost, steady execution, memory and cache behavior under the same correctness conditions.
Include branch/SIMD/atomic/callback cases only as the declared subset supports them; set comparison criteria before selecting results.
acceptance: All declared correctness cases pass on both compared implementations or their differences are explicitly disqualifying.
Versioned results explain tradeoffs and do not extrapolate a scalar benchmark to Megabonk.
A continue/stop decision identifies an advantage relevant to E01 or retains the existing engine.

issues.title: Test the experimental CPU runtime on signed macOS
issues.purpose: A command-line JIT demo does not establish the guest runtime obligations required by a game.
scope: Proceed only if E02 justifies continuation; reuse the P02 host-capability evidence where applicable.
Add guest-state reconstruction, precise faults, code invalidation across threads, native callbacks and executable-memory publication.
Exercise independent memory-order litmus/stress tests and signed-app behavior.
acceptance: Required subset behavior is repeatable under documented normal macOS permissions.
Missing semantics and unsupported host states fail explicitly and remain visible.
A no-go result may close this research item as not planned with rationale; it never counts as implementation success.

issues.title: Integrate the experimental CPU module with Wine
issues.purpose: An independent CPU engine must meet the existing Wine/ARM64EC boundary without recreating Windows APIs.
scope: Proceed only after E03 passes and the same Wine boundary is qualified with the reference FEX path.
Implement thread lifecycle, TLS, exception contexts and native-call/callback transitions with explicit ABI stubs where needed.
Run the shared small PE suite before graphics or Megabonk, keeping backend identity explicit.
acceptance: The declared Wine integration fixture suite passes with complete module provenance and no Rosetta host fallback.
Cranelift AppleAarch64/WindowsFastcall support is not substituted for actual ARM64EC boundary tests.
Any unsupported required ABI operation blocks promotion; results remain labeled experimental.

issues.title: Decide whether to adopt a Pear CPU translator
issues.purpose: Replacing the CPU engine must improve an evidenced constraint while preserving the product's compatibility and maintenance contract.
scope: Run the same full-game, process, save/relaunch and controlled-quality validation as the qualified FEX baseline.
Compare cold/warm behavior, failures, frame times, memory and power where repeatable; include maintainability and source/distribution costs.
Record adoption, further research, or retention of FEX, with evidence and a rollback plan.
acceptance: The decision cites the original hypothesis, like-for-like results and remaining compatibility gaps.
No replacement is promoted before equivalent required-feature qualification; a negative decision is a valid completed research outcome.
If earlier experiments stopped, close conditional implementation items as not planned and document why R1 concluded without a new engine.
